subject: math
cluster: Angles, radian measure, and the unit circle
description: Students define the unit circle as the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ centered at the origin, and use it to evaluate trigonometric functions at standard angles (multiples of $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$, i.e. multiples of $\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{\pi}{4}$). For an angle $\theta$ in standard position, the terminal point on the unit circle is $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$, so they identify exact coordinates and read off exact values of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, and $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$. They use reference angles and quadrant sign rules to extend the first-quadrant values to all four quadrants and to coterminal/negative angles.
subSkills: State the definition of the unit circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ and that a point on it satisfies $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$
Memorize and reproduce first-quadrant exact values for $\theta = 0, \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}$
Determine the reference angle for any standard angle in any quadrant
Apply quadrant sign rules (ASTC) to assign correct signs to $\sin$, $\cos$, $\tan$
Read off the coordinates $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ of the terminal point for a standard angle
Compute $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and recognize where it is undefined
Convert between degree and radian measure for standard angles ($30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}$, etc.)
Reduce coterminal and negative angles to a standard angle in $[0, 2\pi)$ before evaluating

problemArchetypes.name: Evaluate a single function at a standard angle
problemArchetypes.example: Find the exact value of $\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}$. (Reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ in Quadrant II, sine positive: $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Identify terminal-point coordinates
problemArchetypes.example: Give the coordinates of the point where the terminal side of $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}$ meets the unit circle. (Answer: $\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Reference angle and quadrant sign
problemArchetypes.example: State the reference angle and the sign of $\cos\frac{7\pi}{4}$, then evaluate. (Reference $\frac{\pi}{4}$, Quadrant IV, cosine positive: $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Tangent and undefined values
problemArchetypes.example: Find $\tan\frac{\pi}{2}$ and explain. ($\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0$, so $\tan\frac{\pi}{2}$ is undefined.)

problemArchetypes.name: Negative or coterminal angle reduction
problemArchetypes.example: Find $\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$. (Coterminal with $\frac{5\pi}{3}$ or use even symmetry: $\frac{1}{2}$.)

Easy.description: Direct recall of a first-quadrant value or a quadrantal value. Angle is one of $0, \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}$ (or $0^\circ$ through $90^\circ$ equivalents). No reference angle or sign work needed; one step.
constraints: Angle lies in Quadrant I or on a positive axis (multiple of $\frac{\pi}{2}$)
Single function value or a single coordinate requested
All signs are positive (or a clean $0$/$1$/undefined at a quadrantal angle)

Medium.description: Angle lies in Quadrant II, III, or IV. Student must find the reference angle and apply the correct sign via ASTC, then evaluate. Two steps: locate quadrant + assign sign + recall reference value.
constraints: Requires a reference-angle computation and a sign decision
May ask for the terminal-point coordinates (both signed components) or $\tan\theta$ as a quotient

Hard.description: Multi-step: reduce a negative or large coterminal angle (e.g. $> 2\pi$) to standard position first, or combine multiple function values, or state both coordinates plus $\tan\theta$ including undefined cases. May require degree/radian conversion before evaluating.
constraints: Angle is negative, exceeds $2\pi$, or stated in degrees needing conversion (e.g. $-\frac{4\pi}{3}, \frac{13\pi}{6}, 405^\circ$)
Requires coterminal reduction to $[0, 2\pi)$ before reference-angle work
Combines two or more steps, e.g. compute $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, then $\tan\theta$, or identify an undefined tangent

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student swaps sine and cosine on the terminal point, treating the coordinate as $(\sin\theta, \cos\theta)$ instead of $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$
Student ignores the quadrant and keeps the first-quadrant (positive) value, dropping the negative sign
Student confuses the $\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{\pi}{3}$ values, mixing $\frac{1}{2}$ with $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
Student computes the wrong reference angle, subtracting from the wrong axis (uses $\theta - \pi$ in Quadrant II instead of $\pi - \theta$)
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}$ uses reference $\frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3}$ giving $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ instead of reference $\frac{\pi}{6}$ giving $\frac{1}{2}$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student inverts the tangent quotient, computing $\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$ (cotangent) instead of $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$
Student reports a zero-denominator tangent as $0$ rather than undefined
Student treats a negative angle as if it were positive, ignoring the reflection across the $x$-axis
Student mis-converts degrees to radians, scaling by the wrong factor
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Treats $150^\circ$ as $\frac{\pi}{6}$ (reference value) rather than reducing the full angle, giving $\tan 150^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ instead of $-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$
